Shot 2026-11-28 at commit fc22006, High, 1066 x 666, 36 to 42 frames a second, by Tools/unreal/reference_shots.py --area WorldStreet. Numbers: Art/Reference/World/Unreal/WorldStreet.json.

Seen wrong in the game's pictures, for the owner to judge

  • The spot: by Café Asha on the street south of Market Square (x 960, z 915), looking north along it at the reference's eye (1.7 m up), the café's awning and its tables and chairs on the left as in the reference. It replaces an earlier spot by a grocer, where the owner saw "missing chair" (2026-11-28): the café is the place the reference shows. The game's camera is 90 degrees wide where the reference's 22 mm lens sees 79.
  • The buildings are not like the reference's (the owner, 2026-11-28: "some of the structures in the game are not like the ones in the blender. notice the color of wall, windows etc in blender are so much good"). The reference's café has a rough stone ground floor with three large arched windows glowing warm, upper windows evenly spaced with stone surrounds, sills and pairs of louvred shutters, window boxes, an iron balcony, a hanging sign and lit lanterns on posts. The game's has square dark shop windows with nothing seen inside by day, heavier dark window frames, no window boxes, and one lamp post far down the street.
  • The colours are poorer than the reference's (the owner: "review the colors used in these building in the game, the blender has better colors ... the palette and color selection both"). The palette's numbers are the same on both sides (World/rules/building_styles.json and Tools/blender/building_kit_07.py), but (1) selection: this house is warm plaster with ochre shutters and wood frames, tan on tan on brown, and the house opposite bare brown stone, where the reference leads with cool grey plaster and mixes blue, teal and red shutters; (2) the light turns it orange: sunlit plaster measures 191,162,126 here against the reference's neutral 179,175,174, paving 209,197,184 against 191,187,188, and the sky is near white (212,215,218) against the reference's blue (150,165,184), so no cool colour sets off the warm ones; (3) the plaster is a flat fill at this distance and the stone one brown with heavy dark joints (G3, G4).
  • A grey tower block stands over the roofs at the end of the street; the reference's street ends in a wall and a tree.
  • Morning: the look check fails for burnt whites (5 % against 4 %): the sunlit house fronts and the sky white out, and the near paving is a dark brown band (G5).
  • Dusk and night: the café's windows are lit, flat cream panels with nothing seen in them; the paving and the upper walls are near black at dusk under a still-pale sky (G5, G7).
  • Fog whites out: the look check fails it (0.87 stops of light and shade against 1.0).
  • Rain and Fog are pale grey with the warm cast gone; Snow lies as one flat cream sheet; Cloudy still throws hard shadows.
  • Nobody stands in the street near the camera; the reference has people by the café (G6).
  • The paving is small warm brick setts with no kerb where the reference has large grey slabs and a raised kerb.

Seen wrong in the game's pictures, for the owner to judge

  • The spot: under the arch at the east end of the spawn alley (a passage through the houses), looking out on the fountain court behind Market Square, the reference's own eye (1.7 m up, aimed 4.4 degrees up). It replaces the first spot, the look tour's stop on the open stall square, which the owner said was not the right one (2026-11-28). The game's camera is 90 degrees wide where the reference's 24 mm lens sees 74.
  • The place differs from the reference in what is there. The reference stands inside a three-arched arcade with two wall lamps on its piers, on a small paved square with a fountain close by, a bench, a tree and a loggia of lit shop windows across it. The game has one plain arch of a passage with no lamp on it, and beyond it a wide lawned court: the fountain, the trees and the arcaded houses stand far off and small.
  • Rain falls under the roof: in Rain the streaks come down inside the passage, under its arch and the house above it, and in Snow the flakes do too (the owner, 2026-11-28: "water is falling even in the place where there is roof"). The reference's rain and snow fall only under open sky (G8).
  • The arch's stone is a smooth plain cream with no joints or blocks, and the two door leaves standing open in it are plain flat slabs; the walls beside it are rough blocks with heavy joints. The reference's arch is dressed stone throughout (G3).
  • No lamp lights the arch: by day the reference's piers carry warm pools, at dusk and at night its lamps carry the picture. Here the passage at night is lit only by a strip of window light on the left (G7).
  • Nobody stands in the passage or near the arch in any setting; the reference has a person close to the camera and two by the fountain (G6).
  • Midday and Cloudy: the paving beyond the arch is burnt near white, and Cloudy still throws a hard-edged sun patch (G5).
  • Rain and Fog are grey and cold, the warm cast gone; in Rain the stone goes dark grey-green. The reference keeps its warm stone in every weather (G4).
  • Snow lies as one flat cream sheet beyond the arch with no shade in it; the flakes are a few square white dots.
  • Morning: a hard-edged slab of sun lies across the right wall and the paving in the passage; the reference's morning is soft haze.
  • Far things (the houses across the court) fade to pale blue-grey haze at Midday already.

Shot 2026-11-28 at commit e03ba09, High, 1066 x 666, 39 to 46 frames a second, by Tools/unreal/reference_shots.py --area WorldSky. Numbers: Art/Reference/World/Unreal/WorldSky.json.

Seen wrong in the game's pictures, for the owner to judge

  • The spot: in the fountain court behind Market Square (x 900, z 912), 1.7 m up, looking east and 18 degrees up over the roofs, as the reference's camera looks up from its square. The game's camera is 90 degrees wide where the reference's 15 mm lens sees 100.
  • The sky is the weakest part beside the reference: the reference's clouds are large, shaded and layered, grey beneath and white on top, filling the sky; the game's are a few thin soft smears on a pale blue-white ground, with no shading and no depth.
  • Morning's sky is burnt out near white with hardly a cloud to see; Fog, Rain and Snow are one blank pale grey with no cloud at all, where the reference's fog and rain skies are dark, heavy and layered (G5).
  • Cloudy is not overcast: pale sky with thin cloud and the sun still out, the trees lit and throwing shadows. The reference's Cloudy is a full grey deck.
  • Night: a plain dark blue with dim cloud bands and no stars; the reference has stars and moonlit cloud edges. The lawn, the fountain and the trees are near black (G5).
  • Dusk: the sky is pale lilac with soft white cloud, with little of the reference's warm orange under-lighting on the clouds; everything below the roofs is near black, the trees flat black shapes.
  • Rain: the streaks are few and faint against the sky; the trees go dark grey-green and the houses fade to grey.
  • Snow: sparse square white dots; the lawn stays green with no snow lying on it, the roofs, the well or the fountain. The reference's snow lies on every ledge.
  • What is there differs: the reference looks up at a clock tower and a loggia over market stalls and a fountain close by, with people near; here it is a lawned court with trees, a fountain and a well, the houses far off, and nobody in it. Two tree crowns cut into the top corners of the picture.
  • A tower block shows pale behind the left roofs.

The sky over the town, seen from Market Square over the roofs: blue overhead fading to the pale haze at the horizon by day, warm towards the low sun at dusk, the night's dark blue with the town's glow low down; clouds as soft heaps on one layer about 1.2 km up, flat underneath and rounded on top, lit on the sun's side and shaded underneath, pink at dusk, lit from below by the town's lamps at night; how much of the sky they cover follows the weather (clear 0.36, cloudy 0.62, rain 0.97, fog 0.55, snow 0.92); at night the stars, the Milky Way and the full moon's disc. No planet (ADR-0064).

Shot 2026-11-28 at commit 2d9d02b, High, 1066 x 666, 38 to 43 frames a second, by Tools/unreal/reference_shots.py --area WorldAlley. Numbers: Art/Reference/World/Unreal/WorldAlley.json.

Seen wrong in the game's pictures, for the owner to judge

  • The place differs from the reference in what is there. The reference is the alley of Tools/blender/old_town_04.py seen from under a gate arch (its camera 1.7 m up, a 24 mm lens, people facing it): an alley with crates, cloth banners across it, a bridge and a second arch. The game's spawn alley (the look tour's stop, the player from behind, a 90 degree view) is a bare paved lane between two stone houses to an arch on Market Square: no gate arch over the camera, no banners, no crates, nobody but the player.
  • The game's walls are large rough blocks with heavy dark joints and jutting window surrounds; the reference's are smooth dressed stone with fine joints (G3).
  • Nobody else is in the alley in any setting; the reference has six people (G6).
  • Rain, Fog, Snow and Cloudy are grey and cold where the reference keeps its warm stone in every weather: in Rain and Snow the walls go near black, and the warm cast of the look is gone (G4, W4).
  • Fog whites the whole picture out: the look check fails it for too little light and shade (0.94 stops against 1.0) (G5).
  • Snow: flakes fall as large square white dots and no snow lies on the paving, the sills or the bench; the reference has lying snow and small flakes.
  • Rain: the paving shows a few dark puddles but no wet sheen; the streaks are long white lines, heavier than the reference's.
  • At Midday and under cloud the sun's patch on the paving by the arch is burnt white (G5).
  • Cloudy still throws a hard-edged patch of sun on the paving: under cloud there should be none.
  • At night the two wall lanterns are large plain white blocks with no shape, and the lit windows are flat cream panels with nothing seen in them (G7).
  • Dusk reads much lighter than the reference's dusk, and its lit window on the left is burnt.
  • The orange lantern box high on the left wall by day is a plain flat-coloured block (G3).
  • Morning: the sun lies in a large hard patch across the right wall and the paving; the reference's morning alley is in soft haze with no direct sun. Which is right for the hour is the owner's to say.

The look of the world (the old-town alley of style test 02: matte mottled plaster and stone, soft rounded forms, W1-W8) at morning, midday and dusk; at night with the lamps on, and with them off under a full and a new moon; and by day in cloud, rain, fog and snow. No haze at midday. Rain and snow fall, puddles lie with rings where the drops fall into them, and the snow lies, only where the sky is open over them: never under the passage's roof. The kinds of light and their named colours, in a home's room at night

IndoorLightKindsFor your review9 issues seen
Locks
The named colours of light of World/rules/lights.json and the fittings that share them (the owner, 2026-11-26: "when the room is lit by lights then the color should be decided by the light types"; "each colored light should have a name for different styles of lamps, lights, street lights etc. can share the color behavior"). Ten colours: Lantern amber (the palette's Lantern, for street lamps and lanterns to share), Warm white, Soft white, Neutral white, Cool white, Fire red, Neon blue, Neon green, Neon red, Neon amber (the owner: "we also need some cooler and even neon blue and green lights"; "add those 3 suggestions"). Thirteen fittings, each lit alone in the approved home room (IndoorHomeRoom) on a night with no moon and the fire out: floor lamp, table lamp, wall light and pendant in Warm white, desk lamp in Soft white, ceiling light in Neutral white, cool ceiling light in Cool white, wall lantern in Lantern amber, candles in Fire red (every fire one red, candles too: the owner, "Fire red"). Neon is an accent (the owner: "Weaker neon"): a tube of 8 to 10 W, shown with the room's own floor lamp, table lamp and fire lit, so the room keeps its colours and the tube tints its corner. A fitting's strength is its own; its colour is its named colour's. The sheet shows each fitting twice: at one exposure for all (the lamp-lit night's), and with the eye set for that light, at most 2.5 stops either way; each fitting has its own entry under Ornaments (OrnamentsLight<Fitting>), with the second picture.
Approved
proposed 2026-11-26, for the owner to review; pictures at low quality until approved
Decision
ADR-0065, ADR-0067; the owner, 2026-11-26, of the colours and fittings on a trial sheet: "Yes, propose it"

docs/specs/domains/FURNITURE.md 2.5, docs/art/ART_DIRECTION.md 2.3 and 2.6

Seen wrong, for the owner to judge

  • Night only: dusk and the day hours are not shown for these lights.
  • Neon blue, green and red are saturated colours, against the palette rule W4 (muted and warm); allowed as weak accents by the owner's words (ADR-0067).
  • Neon amber is hard to tell from the fire-lit room it is shown in; neon red reads pink and tints more of the room than the other tubes at the same strength.

The shapes are the game's: the court as the mall's plan draws it (World/city_01/blocks/b_16_5.json; Tools/worldgen/mall_inside_01.py, ADR-0038): 92 x 192 m, three floors 6 m apart, the galleries' openings swelling round each atrium and pinching between them, bridges at the pinches, five round roof lights, the moving stairs, fountains, gardens, benches, planters and every outlet's front. The look is its own, from the owner's screenshots of the game's court (Art/StyleTests/mall_wanted_51/) taken further (the owner, 2026-11-26: "feel inspired and take a creative take on the look and feel add ornaments if required use glass and other material"): warm timber slats under the galleries, cream edges with a line of light along each and brass trim, glass balustrades with brass rails, slender cream columns with brass collars, plants hanging over the balustrades; a uniform polished stone floor of large tiles with hidden joints (the owner: "smoother and shiny", "hide the tile edges"), a brass inlay tracing the galleries' curves; the roof lights lightly tinted with a diamond lattice, a chandelier of globes and translucent banners hanging in each; grass islands in white kerbs with trees and flowers; moving stairs with dark treads, glass sides and brass rails; shop fronts with their signs in coloured glass, lit (MallsEastgateShop, ADR-0071). In the world's light: by day the sun and sky through the roof lights, the hidden lights under the edges low; at dusk and at night those at full in the hall lantern's warm white. No moonlit nights, no weather.
Approved
2026-11-26, the owner
Decision
the owner, 2026-11-26: "there will be more reference for mall required for screenshot in attached pics"; "use the shapes from the game for the mall interiors but texture, color, styling etc, please come up with your self"; "Approve it"; ADR-0038, ADR-0061, ADR-0066; made again with the glass shop signs, the owner, 2026-11-28: "Yes, every shop", "Approve, all four" (ADR-0071)

The light fittings as objects, in the four style lines

OrnamentsLightLinesFor your review10 issues seen
Locks
Every light fitting of World/rules/lights.json as an object, laid out as the furniture lines are (the owner, 2026-11-26, with the picture of FurnitureLines: "i wanted this kind of reference"; "some thing that can be transported easily into unreal"): each a piece made as the furniture kits' pieces are, in Plain, Old Town, Workshop and Curve, standing in daylight with a person for scale. Three sheets, 27 fittings. Standing (on a floor or a table): floor lamp, arc floor lamp, table lamp, desk lamp, table lantern, candles, candelabra. Hung (on a wall or a ceiling): wall light, wall lantern, string lights, pendant, chandelier, ceiling light, ceiling panel, track spots, neon ring, and neon tubes in blue, green, red and amber. Street (the street's and the shops'; the owner: "may be we should not leave out street lamps or shop fittings. only mall fitting can be left out"): street lamp, square lamp, a wall lantern for a house wall, bollard light, a shop's sign and its lamp, shop pendant, shelf light. The home fittings are for the buying catalogue (the owner: "can you add more of these lights. all of these will be made available in buying catalog"). How each lights a room, its colour and the way its light falls, is on the room pictures (OrnamentsLight<Fitting>) and the colour sheet (Indoor, IndoorLightKinds).

How the references are kept

  • Every approved look reference is in Art/Reference/<Category>/, named <Category><Subject>[_<Variant>].<ext> in PascalCase: Indoor/IndoorHomeRoom_Morning.jpg, Vehicles/VehiclesSoftBox.png. A reference's id is the name without the variant.
  • Art/Reference/catalog.json is the one list: what each locks, its approval and decision, the script that makes it, the game models built from it, issues seen, its old names. Agents read it there.
  • This page is written from it by python Tools/reference_catalog.py, which first checks that every file is listed and named by the rule. Never edit the page by hand.
  • A new reference: render it with its script, put it in its category's folder under its name, add it to the catalog, run the script. Changing the look needs a new ADR and the owner's approval (ADR-0004).
  • A place with light settings (morning, midday, dusk, the nights, the weathers) shows one Blender picture for what it is, and its settings as pictures taken in the game (ADR-0075): Art/Reference/<Category>/Unreal/<Id>_<Setting>.jpg, written by python Tools/unreal/reference_shots.py --all from the reference's unreal block in the catalog. They are for the owner's review until the owner approves them; a setting the game cannot show is listed as not in the game yet. The Blender settings stay in the folder and in the catalog.
  • A reference taken out of use moves to Art/Retired/ and is listed under Retired.
  • Look tests and rejected ideas stay in Art/StyleTests/; they are not references.
